purpose: Strict JSON rulebook for KiCad V1 visual project generation.
supported_scope: local net labels and SPICE directive text
broad project-local symbols for switches, diodes, LEDs, transistors, regulators, op-amps, counters, shift registers, display drivers, muxes, adders, comparators, and common 40xx/74HC logic ICs
source-guided schematic writing using bundled KiCad source references and mined exact core symbols where available

component_object.id: Unique reference like R1, C1, L1, V1, I1, G1
component_object.kind: one of component_kinds below; core exact symbols are R, L, VDC, VSIN, GND, while broad kinds are emitted as project-local symbols when exact mined symbols are unavailable
component_object.value: display/simulation value such as 1k, 100n, 10m, 10, 1m, AC 1, SIN(0 1 1k)
component_object.at: optional [x,y] in millimeters; omit for automatic topology placement
component_object.rotation: optional degrees; omit for generator defaults
component_object.pins: map KiCad pin number strings to net names, e.g. {"1":"VIN","2":"GND"}

pin_rules.broad_project_local: Use numeric pin strings from the part package or chosen functional mapping. Omitted pins remain visually unconnected. Same net names connect by wire trunks or repeated KiCad local labels.

net_rules: Use readable net names such as VIN, OUT, N1, N2, TANK, LOAD.
All electrical pins on V1-supported components must be assigned.
A same net name means those pins are electrically connected.
Do not create visual-only component zoos for circuit requests.
kicad_writer_rules: The generated .kicad_pro is the file the user opens.
The matching .kicad_sch is generated beside it.
Every wire object must have exactly two xy points.
All wires must be horizontal or vertical.
Wires terminate exactly on pin endpoints, junctions, or same-net trunks.
Symbols are embedded in the project schematic; V1 exact symbols are source-pack mined where available.
Rails and broad digital bus/control nets may use repeated local labels instead of long sheet-spanning wires.
